actions.name: drive forward at 10 % without a distance

control_flow: stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, drive forward at 10 %; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line, and when a wall is right in front, stop before touching it and stay there.

decision_points.condition: an obstacle is ahead (front infrared sensor)

branches.outcome: an obstacle is ahead: it drives forward at 10 %
no obstacle ahead: it follows the line
black under the line tracker: it curves left

scenarios.coded_response: It drives forward at 10 % into the wall; nothing stops the motors
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is on a black line in bright light, and a wall is in front of it, either further along the line or right in front at the start
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall
scenarios.title: Stops before the wall in front
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without touching it, and stays there

uncertainties: You said it should stop, but no block stops the motors: with a wall ahead the program drives forward at 10 % and bumps into it.
You didn't say where the line ends or what the robot should do there, so the end of the line is taken as the goal.
The forever loop calls the function many times a second, so the line tracker and the obstacle sensor are read very often; the simulator is fine with that.
